A first look at a meal-prep service

Fictional example, prepared to show the format of a deliverable. No client work, research, message sending or automation was performed by opening this page.

Scope: one hypothetical home-based meal-prep service in one local delivery area. Stage: idea exploration.

The idea

Prepare a small weekly menu for customers who want convenient lunches. The exact offer, location, production capacity and business requirements are not yet confirmed.

Audience hypothesis

Nearby office workers may be a useful first audience. This is an assumption to test, not evidence of demand. Other audiences may have different budgets, dietary needs and delivery expectations.

Questions before spending

  1. Who would buy, how often, and what do they currently use instead?
  2. What complete costs apply to one order, including packaging and delivery?
  3. Which local permissions, food-handling requirements and production arrangements must be confirmed with the relevant authorities?
  4. What delivery radius and order volume can the business reliably support?

A small validation plan

Speak with a small group of potential customers using the same neutral questions. Compare their preferences with realistic production and delivery costs. If requirements allow, plan a limited pilot with a clear menu, confirmed price and feedback process before a larger launch.

First deliverables to consider

  • A one-page offer and enquiry form.
  • Approved menu and business information.
  • A simple order-and-expense tracker.
  • A small batch of launch captions using only verified claims.

Evidence and limits

This fictional example contains no market research, public-source findings, sales forecast or profitability conclusion. In an accepted trial brief, supplied facts, any public sources consulted and unresolved gaps would be identified separately. A full feasibility study is outside this short sample.
